chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Abu al-Maghra' said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is behind the Imam, who makes a mistake (in prayer) and thus prostrates for forgetfulness before the Imam prostrates, he said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.اَلسَّهْو: Mistake or forgetfulness in prayer leading to extra or missing actions
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm; it is permissible/valid
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: Here used in the context of performing the prostration (sujud) for forgetfulness

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a follower performs the prostration of forgetfulness before the Imam in prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a follower’s premature prostration of forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle of flexibility in congregational rites. This ruling underscores the practical leniency granted to the *ma'mum* to maintain unity with the Imam, even if minor procedural discrepancies occur due to human error.
